ZU67DR Pulse Array

Four modules, each a HamGeek XCZU67DR card on a custom AFE carrier, drive 32 RF-DAC columns and 32 one-bit rows: 1 MHz – 5 GHz target, 3 V into 50 Ω, one shared 5 MHz clock.

Details How the snapshot is computed

The snapshot and the requirements strip only format model results; nothing is computed on this stage.

  • PA.calc(): modules, outputs, power, PSU, rack U, sync profile and cables (Power, Mechanical / rack).
  • PA.model.freq.rates(freqPreset): GTY and RF-DAC rates, UI, Ts, SYSREF period (Frequency plan).
  • PA.model.pulse.compare(τ, rates): bits and samples per pulse (Pulse generation).
  • PA.model.summary(c, state): the six status chips and the open risks; each chip opens its owner stage.
  • PA.explain(field) and the model calc objects: every ⓘ and the Calculation block.

Array sizes → Sync options compared →

Details Derived and true SYSREF, one build

Every module is built the same, so a sync option is a cable-selected profile: rear cables plus a software profile. The options are a sync unit, any module as root through a passive splitter, or a daisy chain; one module is the bench profile with no sync cables.

Derived SYSREF (the default): each card makes its own SYSREF from the shared 5 MHz CLK in nested zero-delay mode. True SYSREF: the same 5 MHz edge reaches each card's SYNC pin through J27 → card J64, over the same cables. The period is 200 ns in both.

The choice carries through power, cable count, rack height and the 3D model. The control PC, a Minisforum MS-A2 on the Ethernet switch, only uploads patterns, sets DC levels and reads back status.

Engineering notes Block notes for every part of the diagram
Control PC
A small PC, a Minisforum MS-A2 (≈ 196 × 189 × 48 mm, vendor figure, check), sits next to the Ethernet switch on the bench or on the shared 2U rack shelf. It runs the web UI and Python API. It uploads patterns to every card over Gigabit Ethernet, sets the DC levels and reads back status. Nothing timing-critical passes through it; the card hands DC-level and attenuator settings on to the carrier over its GPIO header.
GbE switch
One GbE switch port per card plus one for the PC: 5 ports, so an 8-port switch.
Clock source (Sync unit (1U))
A 1U box: an OCXO-referenced LMK04832 sends CLK (5 MHz), SYSREF and a re-timed TRIG to every module over phase-matched coax in a star (3 cables per module, 2 with derived SYSREF). SYSREF: derived, so each card makes its own from the shared 5 MHz CLK in nested zero-delay. Each card’s own J32 (250 MHz) comes back through its carrier as the GTY reference, so all outputs share one time base. Changing the option means re-plugging rear cables and loading a profile; the cards then re-sync and re-run MTS.
HamGeek XCZU67DR card
One PCIe card per module holds the pattern memory, the sequencer and the sync logic. Its eight RF-DACs and eight GTY transmitters make every output in the array.
RF-DAC, 8 per card
Eight 14-bit RF-DACs run at up to 10 GS/s and make arbitrary waveforms for this card’s 8 columns (32 in the array). They leave the card on SSMC J44–J51 and reach the carrier over eight SSMC jumpers. The on-card balun limits the low end to about 30 MHz until it is swapped or bypassed.
GTY serializer, 8 per card
Eight GTY transmitters run as 20 Gb/s serializers, which gives a 50 ps grid for the one-bit rows. They reach the carrier through the PCIe x8 edge. Only TX0–3 are routed there as delivered, so TX4–7 need a rework of 8 capacitors.
RF-ADC, 8 per card
The eight RF-ADCs are not part of the output path. They stay spare for a skew check (loop an output back and measure it) and are not in the multi-tile sync. Access: rear access cover (cables through its brush-strip slot with the cover on, cover off to plug).
GTY reference loop
Card J32 (250 MHz, the card’s only SMA) → coax W23 → carrier J45 → C20 → U27 LMK1D1204 → PCIE_CLK pins: the GTY reference of quads A and B, in every sync profile.
AFE carrier
Our carrier takes the card upright in a vertical PCIe x8 slot (Gen5-rated); the slot latch and four M3 standoffs to the right wall hold it. It amplifies the DAC and one-bit outputs to 3 V into 50 Ω, adds a DC level per channel through bias tees, and buffers the card’s 250 MHz J32 clock back into the slot as the GTY reference. Its clock zone (three LMK00804B buffers, a Y1 TCXO ÷ 2 and an I²C expander) is the same on every carrier, and software picks the clock source for each sync option.
One-bit AFE
Each one-bit output is a symmetric A / B pair: the two GTY legs run mirrored through HMC788A gain stages into the balun, then a bias tee adds the DC level.
J65 ribbon
A 2×10 ribbon from the card's J65 header to carrier J31 carries ten 3.3 V I/O lines and I²C. The card uses it to set the DC-level DACs and the step attenuators on the carrier.
12 V supply
One 12 V supply feeds every carrier in a star, and each carrier passes 12 V on to its card through the slot (and P3 if the card needs more). The power budget for the chosen module count is in Power.
DUT array
With 4 modules the array drives 32 RF-DAC columns and 32 one-bit rows at 3 V into 50 Ω. The requirement is 32 + 32 (four modules); 8 + 8 or 16 DAC fit one or two modules, and eight modules give 64 + 64. Mechanical / rack compares the options.

Details Why no CML receiver

The one-bit chain has no separate CML receiver or level translator. The GTY output is already CML, and every extra stage adds jitter and slows the edges.

Each leg gets one gain block (HMC788A class, about 16 dB), and the T1 balun combines the P and N legs. The single-ended option uses one leg and terminates the other in 49.9 Ω; it is the only intended asymmetry.

Carrier blockRole
One-bit front end ×8Takes the GTY lanes from J1, amplifies each leg (HMC788A) and combines them in a UWB2-50E balun, or uses one leg. The eight cells (15 mm pitch, one can) sit between J1 and the rear edge, so the 20 Gb/s lanes stay short and each output launches straight into its rear-panel jack.
RF-DAC front end ×8Takes each DAC output from its SSMC jumper, then equalises, attenuates and amplifies it to 3 V into 50 Ω. A bias tee sets the DC level. Each output leaves on a vertical SMPM and one identical pigtail to its rear-panel bulkhead.
Control and monitoringI²C / SPI from card J65: DC-level DACs for the bias tees, attenuator control, rail V / I, temperature and board ID.
Clock and syncJ26 / J27 → U20 / U22 (LMK00804B) → card J35 / J64; U28 drives J29 (Y1 ÷ 2 root, relay of J26 in a chain, or off). A TCA9538 on the J65 I²C sets every source. J28 → D11 → U62 → slot A11. Card J32 returns on J45; U27 makes the GTY reference.
Carrier powerJ30 on the rear panel feeds 12 V over a short lead to J46, then the slot (≤ 66 W by the PCIe spec) and the AFE rails through bucks and LDOs, with sequencing and power-good to the card.

Holes and hardware: Ø6.5 hole with one 5.9 mm flat (D-flat, anti-rotation); internal-tooth lock washer (≤ Ø11.9) + 5/16 in panel nut outside; thread past the outer face ≥ 7.0 mm (washer (0.6) + nut (2.4) + 4.0 plug engagement). Retention: pull panel nuts (flange / clamp face on the panel inner face); side D-flat holes; push carrier supports + row A panel nuts; torque: the panel takes the torque.

Row A part (part to confirm): 1/4-36 D-flat thread ≥ 9.5 mm from the clamp face; axis 4.6 ± 0.1 mm above the PCB; clamp face 1.0 mm beyond the footprint edge (carrier edge at −D/2 + 3, flange on the panel inner face); flange ≤ 1.0 mm thick; centre-pin tail ≤ 0.5 mm below the board; VSWR ≤ 1.3 to 10 GHz on the footprint.

J30 12V IN: panel-mount 2 × 2 Micro-Fit 3.0-class plug housing (male pins in a shroud, keyed, latch ramp up; check the series, local 1.5 mm spot-face if its ears need it) + carrier entry header J46; the external star lead ends in a 2 × 2 receptacle with the latch; lead 4 × 18 AWG ≤ 100 mm to J46 (two per rail; Micro-Fit 3.0 crimps cover 18–30 AWG); ≈ 8.5 A per contact (catalogue), ≈ 6 A per circuit after multi-circuit derating (check the Molex chart): 2 circuits per rail. panel cut-out for the 2 × 2 Micro-Fit 3.0-class plug housing (from the housing drawing: check the series; local 1.5 mm spot-face if its ears need it); latch up.

Assembly: solder J18–J25 with the rear panel (or a CNC copy with the same holes and the carrier mounting holes) bolted at the seated position, nuts finger-tight; keep panel + carrier as a serialised pair; in the box: carrier in with the rear panel off and its screws loose; slide the panel +z over the 8 threads; panel screws; washers + nuts to torque; carrier screws last; removal: unmate the SMPM pigtails, take off the 8 nuts, slide the panel back ≥ 10 mm, lift the carrier.

rear access cover: a cable plate over the SSMC access window (x +62 … +80, y 25 … 166), four captive M3, one 6 mm slot with brush-strip edge trim for ADC1–8 and a Ø6 hole for J57, so the cables run with the cover on. Finish: chromate conversion MIL-DTL-5541 Type II Class 3, or anodized with masked Ø12 lands at every RF hole and a 5 mm land around the window; internal-tooth lock washers. DAC-only build: J18–J25 not fitted, their 8 D-flat holes capped (21 positions still drilled).

No length here changes with the card length L: L moves only the front panel and the buck zone. The one-bit outputs launch straight from the carrier edge into row A; the RF-DAC outputs and the sync inputs reach the rear panel over the pigtails. Lengths come from PA.model.geom.

Sync cables for UNIT-DZ: 8 (CLK 4, SYSREF 0, TRIG 4). The clock zone on every carrier adds ≈ 0.4 W (estimate), and the sync unit ≈ 10 W.

Assumptions Card measurements (±3 %)

The card size comes from the vendor photos: about 235 × 148 mm (±3 %), measured against the x8 edge fingers, the QSFP cages and the RJ45; the top-left corner follows the real-board photo (SSMC column from the top: J57 GNSS_ANT, J64 PPS_IN, J35 CLK1_IN, then DAC7 J51, DAC6 J49, DAC5 J47). The other dimensions are estimates.

The CLK path needs no rework: J35 reaches LMK CLKin1 through R345, R348 and C374 as fitted. The one-time card tweak, the same on every card, is for true SYSREF only: remove R699 and fit one jacketed 1.13 mm micro-coax of one fixed length (45–70 mm expected, ± 2 mm) from the J64 centre-finger joint to the LMK-side pad of R699 (LMK SYNC pin 6), across the empty U101 GNSS footprint on Kapton. R245, R248 and the ESD part stay, so FPGA A10 becomes an input-only SYSREF monitor. Where R699 sits and the coax length are checked on the first card; if R699 cannot be reached cleanly, the modules run derived SYSREF only, with no soldering.

The card has no I/O bracket (the photos show a bare board on four corner standoffs), so the box holds it by its four corner holes. It stands at the right wall with its SSMC edge to the rear, 32 mm inside the rear panel, its I/O to the front and its component side toward −x. The vendor standoffs come off; four M3 F-F hex standoffs of 8 mm plus a 0.7 mm shim bridge the 8.7 mm from the card's back face to the right wall: an M3 × 5 screw from the component side, an M3 × 6 pan head with a Ø9 washer from outside the wall through a Ø5 hole that takes ± 1 mm. The slot latch holds the card down (it needs the retention notch on the x8 tab: check), and the plug forces of the QSFP and RJ45 go into the wall, not into the slot contacts. The screw heads stand up to 3.2 mm proud of the right wall, so neighbouring boxes on a bench sit 4 mm apart.

The corner holes are photo estimates at (u, v) = (7.6, 4.6) and (228, 5) along the top edge, (9.2, 149.7) in the corner tab under ADC0 and (228, 143) at the bottom front: measure the two bottom holes and the tab on the first card.

Insertion, lid off: plug W23 onto J45 first. Hold the card at least 7 mm toward the rear, lower it to 10.5 mm above the seat, slide it forward and press it into J1; the SSMC barrels stay clear of the rear panel during the slide, and the QSFP cages and the power-switch lever stay inside the front cut-out. Fit the four wall screws, then D0–D7, W21, W22, W23 at the card, the ribbon, the I/O shield and the lid. Removal is the reverse.

Measure the card when it arrives and enter its length above (225–320 mm): the front panel moves and the buck zone stretches; the lanes, the cables and every part referenced to the rear stay where they are.

Engineering notes Thermal paths and estimates

Standard box · inlet ≈ 7 167 mm²

  • front to rear: front inlet field with filter (x −78 … +50, y 16 … 150) → bucks, clock, control → card heatsink (card fan) → 60 mm rear exhaust fan; the RF cans at the rear sit in the flow toward the fan; ≈ 9.6 K air rise at 32 W (estimate)
  • Tj ≈ 83 °C at 32 W card power in 35 °C room air, closed lid (estimate).
  • closed-lid temperatures (card, RF cans, bucks): TO MEASURE on the first build (to measure)

Cooling (estimates): the front inlet with its filter, the card fan on the heatsink and one 60 mm rear exhaust fan; the RF cans sit at the rear in the flow toward the fan. Confirm in a closed-lid test.

Engineering notes J1 Gen5 vertical socket: part and footprint

J1 is a vertical x8 CEM socket rated PCIe Gen5 (32 GT/s), SMT preferred so it can be backdrilled; the part is still to confirm. Its housing is centred on the card plane at the right wall, pin 1 toward the rear. The card's TX pairs leave the tails on side A and escape under the housing toward −x on L3; REFCLK and TRIG enter from below on L6.

Before the carrier freezes: pick the part and check its footprint, the housing height (drawn 13.6–24 mm) and the retention latch against the x8 tab. Get the S-parameter model, measure a VNA/TDR coupon (10 MHz–10 GHz) and run a 20 Gb/s pulse test through the real connector. Pass: S11 ≤ −15 dB with a smooth S21 to 5–6 GHz, S11 ≤ −10 dB to 8 GHz, NEXT/FEXT between adjacent TX pairs ≤ −35 dB, and clean pulse edges at the cell input.

Also open before the freeze: the 12 V current through J1 (above 4 A fit the J34 lead), the heatsink fin direction and the closed-lid temperature.

Pulse generation

The one-bit path draws a pulse from GTY bit cells, the RF-DAC path from fewer, wider DAC samples.

20 Gb/sGTY line rateone bit 50 ps
10 GS/sRF-DAC rateone sample 100 ps
500 psPulse width τ
10Bits per pulsewhole bits
5DAC samples per pulsewhole samples
5 GHzNyquistsinc −3.92 dB
Rates (frequency plan preset, shared)
Width on the one-bit grid PASS10 × 50 psWidth on the DAC grid PASS5 × 100 psDAC response at Nyquist INFO−3.92 dB at 5 GHzTiming step PASSone-bit 50 ps

The DAC defines a 500 ps pulse with 5 samples, the one-bit path with 10 bits; above ≈ 4.4 GHz the DAC sinc loses more than 3 dB.

Details Formulas · why NRZ · images and FL1
QuantityFormulaNow
Bits per pulsenbit = τ · R = τ / UI500 / 50 = 10.00
DAC samples per pulsens = τ · fs = τ / Ts500 / 100 = 5.00
NyquistfN = fs / 25 GHz
DAC hold response|H(f)| = |sin(πf / fs) / (πf / fs)|−2.42 dB at 4 GHz, −3.92 dB at 5 GHz, −3 dB at 4.43 GHz
Imagefimg = fs − f4 GHz → 6 GHz, only 3.5 dB below the wanted tone

The RF-DAC holds each sample for one period (NRZ, zero-order hold). The hold shapes the spectrum with |sinc|, so 5 GHz, the Nyquist frequency at 10 GS/s, sits 3.92 dB down.

Each tone f also appears as an image at fs − f. FL1 on the carrier is a low-pass with a rising EQ: it removes the images above Nyquist and flattens the sinc droop (design target, not yet modelled).

The one-bit path has no hold: a GTY bit is a full-swing NRZ cell of one UI, so a pulse edge moves in 50 ps steps without changing its shape.

A width off the DAC grid can be approximated by giving the edge sample a fractional amplitude (sub-sample shaping). It moves the half-amplitude crossing at the cost of a slower edge; not validated here.

    Details Clock-plan rules (PG269, DS926, LMK04828)
    • The DAC AXI4-Stream clock comes from PL_CLK through an MMCM, never from clk_dacX. PG269 p.188↗ PG269 p.190↗
    • PL_CLK 125 MHz × 5 = 625 MHz is an integer ratio, but PG269 says "common integer multiple" and every AMD example is a power of two: Vivado check before any board work. PG269 p.224↗ PG269 p.359↗
    • Fabric clocks stay at or below 500 MHz; the 625 MHz DAC AXI domain is the one exception, so check its timing closure on the −2 part. DS926↗
    • SYSREF stays below 10 MHz and a whole sub-multiple of every clock that samples it. PG269 p.187–188↗
    • The card LMK04828 makes every clock from one VCO: PLL1 locks to CLK IN in zero-delay mode, PLL2 sets the VCO; the register values need a TICS Pro check. datasheet↗ TI TICS Pro↗

    What changes between options: only these cables

    • The rear cables on J26, J27, J28 and J29, and the external splitter(s) and TRIG star.
    • The profile each module gets from the PC: root flag, U30 settings, DZ or TS5, TRIG drive or listen.
    • Inside the box nothing moves: W17–W23 are fixed in every profile.
    • After any re-cable, relock or profile change: re-sync the cards and re-run MTS (PG269 p.163, p.185–186).

    Every card and every carrier is built the same way; any module can be the root. Card prep: Card findings (one-time card prep checklist). Bench risks and checks, in order: Roadmap & open items.

    Details Why a SYSREF-gated start: trigger simulator

    TRIG reaches each module a few ns apart because cables and receivers differ. With SYSREF gating the trigger only arms the module and all modules start on the next SYSREF edge. Starting straight on TRIG copies the arrival spread into the outputs, rounded to the 8 ns sample clock of D9 (PL_CLK 125 MHz).

    TRIG arrives armed, waiting pattern start SYSREF edge (every 200 ns) 8 ns D9 sample clock (zoom)
    0 psstart spread between modules
    0 nsTRIG arrival spread

    Details Bring-up registers and the clock tree

    Steps 1–9 match the Bring-up columns of the timing diagram. Pick a step to see the blocks it uses in the clock tree (the sync-unit star, UNIT-TS; other profiles use Y1 + U29 on one carrier or a lab generator as the root).

    1. The PC sends each module its profile. The PS writes U30 over I²C (enable off, change the source, enable on), so no runt pulse reaches a card. Exactly one root: Y1 and LOCAL5 on one module, or the sync unit, or a lab generator.
    2. Every U20 passes CLK (J26, or LOCAL5 on a bench module) to card J35. U28 sends J29: LOCAL5 on the root, a relay of J26 in a chain, off on leaves and on the tail. U22 holds the card SYNC pin low.
    3. Each card LMK04828 locks PLL1 to CLK on J35 (CLKin1: CLKin_SEL_MODE = 1, CLKin1_OUT_MUX = PLL1, bipolar, CLKin0 off) and PLL2 to its VCXO, first in dual-loop (CLKin1_R = 25, PLL1_N = 96, 0.2 MHz PFD). Our register file owns the LMK: it clears the vendor HOLDOVER_FORCE and MAN_DAC_EN and fixes OSCin_FREQ. The PS reads RB_PLL1_LD and RB_PLL2_LD over SPI. LOS does not work on a bipolar input, so the FPGA counts MON_CLK to catch a lost reference.
    4. Divider sync. DZ: SPI sync (SYNC_POL toggle, SYNC_MODE = 1) in dual-loop with the pin held low, then nested zero-delay (CLKin1_R = 1, PLL1_NCLK_MUX = 1, FB_MUX = 2 SYSREF divider, PLL1_N = 1), then SYNC_MODE = 0 so the pin is ignored. TS5: nested zero-delay with DCLKout8 feedback (FB_MUX = 1, PLL1_N = 25, UG1437 p.10), SYNC_1SHOT_EN = 1, SYNC_DIS8 = 1 (the feedback divider is not reset) and SYNC_DISX = 0 only on DAC_REFCLK (6, 12), the SDCLKs and SYSREF. U61 passes exactly one 5 MHz edge (U22 → W22 → J64 → coax → SYNC pin), timed from MON_CLK; A10 and MON_SYNC each count 1. Then SYNC_DISX = 1 and SYSREF_MUX = 3 (continuous) or the pulser. The TS5 corrections are to check against UG1437, and the edge placement is set by a per-module trim scan (to measure). Then wait a fixed settle time (≥ 10 loop time constants, from PLLatinum), not lock detect alone.
    5. Release the MMCMs (PL_CLK 125 MHz → 625 MHz DAC AXI, 250 MHz fabric), then the GTY QPLL0: card J32 250 MHz → W23 → J45 → U27 → PCIE_CLK, N = 40.
    6. Each card runs RF-DAC MTS with target −1 and reports its latency (PG269 p.186).
    7. The PC sets one common target: the largest latency seen over ≥ 5 power cycles plus 16 samples. MTS runs again and must return XRFDC_MTS_OK; the PC compares it with the value stored for this profile and cable set.
    8. GTY lanes come up with TX buffer bypass and phase alignment; the PL loads the patterns and applies the stored skew table.
    9. TRIG: the TRIG master (the sync unit re-timer, or one FPGA driving D9 → slot A11 PERST# → U62 → its J28) launches 60 ns after its SYSREF edge and zeroes a common 5 MHz period counter. Every module arms on a level-qualified TRIG at D9 and starts on the same SYSREF edge.

    After any re-cable, relock, profile change or RF-DAC Reset Count change: stop, re-sync from step 2 and re-run MTS (PG269 p.163, p.185–186). In multi-module profiles the card LMK runs zero-delay; dual-loop is used only for a moment during the DZ divider sync, because it can lock at 4 or more VCO-grid positions ≈ 83 ps apart.

    Pick a step to see the blocks it uses.

    Carrier clock zone, the same on every carrier

    • U20, U22 and U28 are LMK00804B buffers with an LVCMOS input and a differential input (U22 VDDO 2.5 V from U60). U20 feeds card J35 (CLK), U22 drives card J64 (SYNC, DC-coupled), U28 drives J29.
    • Y1 (10 MHz TCXO with OE) and U29 (÷ 2) make LOCAL5, the 5 MHz root. Only the root turns them on.
    • U30 (TCA9538, I²C 0x70) sets every source. U61 passes the SYNC pin only when U30 P3 and J31 IO3 are both high. U59 holds U20, U22 and U30 off while the card is off.
    • J26 and J27 inputs: −3 dB tap, AC-coupled, idle low. They take square sources of 0.35–1.8 Vpp at 5 or 10 MHz. U27 runs in differential input mode.
    • TRIG: rear-panel J28 → W19 → J28A → D11 TVS → U62 switch (on only with card power good) → 33 Ω → slot A11 PERST#.
    • Removed: U21 with its VCXO, JP1, JP3, J40, J41, J43, K1, the Ethernet option E2 and the PERST# pull-up.

    Parts and nets: Carrier schematic.

    Details Splitter rules and input levels

    A J29 output is 3.3 V behind 50 Ω: 1.65 Vpp into 50 Ω. A transformer splitter loses about 10·log10(n) + 1 dB per stage, and the J26 / J27 network taps −3 dB in front of the LMK00804B. The input window is 0.25–1.3 Vpp after the tap (LMK00804B VID 0.15–1.3 V, check); the highest high level, 2.24 V, stays under the 2.45 V common-mode maximum. U20 restores full swing, so card J35 sees ≈ 1.65 Vpp with fast edges.

    Splitter band: ≤ 1 MHz to ≥ 500 MHz, so the 5 MHz square keeps sub-ns edges. ZFSC-4-1 (1–1000 MHz) for N ≤ 4; for N = 8 a ZSC-2-1+ feeding two ZFSC-4-1, or a wide-band 8-way (check). Not ZFSC-8-1 (0.5–175 MHz, slows the edges) and not ZFSC-2-1 (5–500 MHz, 5 MHz at the band edge). Square sources only, ≥ 0.2 V/ns at the connector; terminate unused ports in 50 Ω and use one cable length to every input, the loop-back included. AC-coupled transport is fine for the continuous SYSREF of MTS (PG269 p.187), not for a pulsed DC-coupled SYSREF.

    Details Card inputs: J35, J64, TRIG IO and J57

    The card's SSMC column (on the edge that faces the rear panel) starts, from the top, with J57 GNSS_ANT, J64 PPS_IN and J35 CLK1_IN, then DAC7 (J51) and down. J32 "CLK_OUT" is the only SMA on the card. J66 and J67 from the V1 schematic do not exist on the real card. TRIG no longer uses this column: it enters through the slot pin PERST#.

    J35 CLK1_IN: the clock input, stock

    J35 → R345 0 Ω → R348 49.9 Ω shunt → C374 0.1 µF → LMK04828 pin 34 CLKin1 (pin 35 AC-grounded through C373). W21 from carrier J32 plugs in with a right-angle SSMC plug and brings ≈ 1.65 Vpp, AC-coupled. No FPGA is in the path, so the reference is there from carrier power-up. Registers only: CLKin_SEL_MODE = 1, CLKin1_OUT_MUX = PLL1, bipolar input. If the first card shows J35 on CLKin0, only the registers change (CLKin_SEL_MODE = 0).

    J64 PPS_IN: the true SYSREF entry, after one tweak

    Stock: J64 → R245 33 Ω → FPGA A10, R248 1 kΩ to ground, U127 ESD. The tweak, identical on every card: remove R699 and fit one jacketed 1.13 mm micro-coax of one fixed length from the J64 centre-finger joint to the LMK-side pad of R699 (net LMK_SYNC, pin 6), across the empty U101 footprint on Kapton. The braid goes to a J64 ground finger and to one fixed ground pad chosen on the first card.

    • W22 from carrier J33 (U22, 2.5 V LVCMOS, 43 Ω, DC-coupled) lands here with a right-angle SSMC plug.
    • R245, R248 and U127 stay. A10 becomes an input-only SYSREF monitor: 1 edge per TS sync, 0 in DZ, compared with MON_SYNC. R248 holds the SYNC pin low when W22 is unplugged.
    • Tap on the J64 side only: an A10-side tap or a shorted R245 gives a slow or ringing edge (idealised simulation; probe the first card).
    • J64 now reaches the LMK pin (abs max 3.6 V): only a ≤ 2.5 V, 50 Ω-source signal goes in.
    • If R699 cannot be reached cleanly: derived SYSREF only, no soldering, and True and Master + 2 splitters are greyed out.
    • The PPS_IN function is given up; a lab PPS enters through J28 → D9.

    TRIG IO: slot PERST# → D9, no card work

    Rear-panel J28 → W19 → J28A → D11 TVS → 50 Ω trace → U62 isolation switch (on only while the card has power) → 33 Ω → slot A11 PERST# → card R242 0 Ω → FPGA D9 (IOBUF, 3.3 V HD bank). The FPGA sets the direction: the TRIG master drives, the others listen.

    • Levels: resistive star or a short bus for N ≤ 4, a 10 kΩ load per module. Above 4: an active TRIG fan-out (≈ $30–60, estimate), the sync unit's TRIG outputs or the GNSS-armed start.
    • Timing: the master launches 60 ns after its SYSREF edge, pulse ≥ 200 ns. Every module arms 48 ns after TRIG reaches D9 (2-flip-flop synchroniser, 4 highs at 125 MHz), at 108–122 ns over every TRIG kit and N: early margin 108–122 ns, late margin 78–92 ns inside the 200 ns window (estimate). On the daisy chain each module is measured against its own SYSREF edge, (k − 1) hops late: early 87–116 ns, late 84–113 ns. DC high at D9 for this set-up: 3.1–3.3 V at D9 against VIH 2 V (estimate). The master uses the same arm rule.
    • D9: SLEW SLOW, DRIVE 8, pull-down. A11 sits two pins from the GTY REFCLK (A13/A14): check QPLL0 during a TRIG edge.
    • First card: rev 2.1 may have a buffer on PERST# (the "_LS" net name); measure the A11 finger and test both directions through the slot.

    J57 GNSS: free; GNSS needs U101

    J57 → NEO-M8N RF_IN, with antenna bias from VCC_RF through L40 10 nH. U101 (the NEO-M8N) is not fitted on the stock card, so J57 stays free and position 0 is clear for an antenna plug. The TIMEPULSE goes only to FPGA pin A9 (GNSS_PPS), not to the LMK: time of day and a PPS of tens-of-ns class (check the datasheet), not a reference for ps alignment.

    Details J32 as GTY reference

    J32 is the vertical SMA on the card's top edge (schematic page 18), and the card's only external clock output.

    • Source. LMK04828 SDCLKOUT5. It shares its clock group with DCLKOUT4 (ADC_REFCLK1, an RF-ADC tile we do not use), so J32 is free. It can be a device clock, VCO ÷ 1 to 32 (≥ 93.75 MHz at VCO1 = 3000 MHz; 250 MHz = ÷ 12), or the SYSREF divider output, VCO ÷ 8 to 8191 (5 MHz = ÷ 600).
    • Electrical. Single-ended, DC-coupled LVPECL: P side through R651 33 Ω with a 240 Ω emitter pull-down (R338), N side to GND through C395 0.1 µF. About 0.4–0.6 Vpp into 50 Ω (estimate), more in the LVPECL 2000 mV format. Needs an inline DC block.

    Yes, as the GTY reference, in every carrier profile

    J32 at 250 MHz → short coax W23 → carrier J45 "GTY REF IN" → C20 DC block → U27 (LMK1D1204) → PCIE_CLK edge pins (10 nF series on the card) → GTY quad A refclk1, shared with quad B. QPLL0 N = 40 → VCO 10 GHz → 20 Gb/s full rate. U27 runs in differential input mode (IN0_P with 49.9 Ω, IN0_N AC-coupled to VAC_REF0): its single-ended LVCMOS mode needs ≥ 0.4 Vpp and stops at 250 MHz, our rate.

    The GTY clock is then locked and phase-fixed to the card's own PL_CLK, DAC and SYSREF clocks: 250 MHz = 50 × 5 MHz has one fixed phase to SYSREF. W23 never moves in any profile.

    Start-up rule. The card LMK locks, syncs and settles before the GTY QPLL is released.

    As a chain clock: only for bare cards

    Card-only chain A1. J32 in SYSREF-divider mode (5 MHz, LVPECL 2000 mV) → DC block → next card J35 (no terminator: R348 already terminates it), derived SYSREF, no carriers. TRIG comes from a ≤ 2.5 V, 50 Ω-source LVCMOS into J64 or from a GNSS start. The GTY then runs from the card's free-running SI5341 (one-bit rows not locked to the DACs). Each card's SPI sync briefly stops its J32, so the cards sync strictly root → tail. Bring-up only; see the Daisy-chain option.

    No carrier profile takes SYSREF from card J32. The legacy two-splitter cabling now feeds both splitters from the root's J29.

    Card plan dividers (VCO1 3000 MHz: DAC_REFCLK ÷ 6, SYSREF ÷ 600, PL_CLK ÷ 24) live in the Frequency plan.

    Details GNSS-armed start
    • To use GNSS: fit U101 on every card as an identical option; the SYNC coax then re-routes below its outline and is re-measured.
    • Antenna feed: rear access cover: J57 GNSS beside ADC1–8, its cable through its own Ø6 hole with the cover on (cover off for plugging). No GNSS jack on the rear panel and no internal GNSS cable.
    • GNSS-armed start: every module arms on the same GNSS second and starts on the first common SYSREF edge after it, so no TRIG cable is needed. The modules still share CLK. If a PPS lands within ≈ 50 ns of a SYSREF edge on any module, the PC moves to the next second.
    • Time stamps and set-ups far apart: common time without a cable between them.

    Details Simulator model · what builds up along a chain

    Simulator. It follows one SYSREF edge down the chain. Each hop adds the cable, the W20 and W17 pigtails and the U28 delay (PA.model.sync.hopNs), and each module's SYSREF capture sits inside one PL_CLK period (125 MHz, 8 ns). The 4 ns fabric clock only sets the start-offset step.

    Drift, reference jitter and the TRIG margins come from PA.model.sync and PA.model.trig. Buffer mismatch comes from a fixed seed, so the same settings always give the same result. The buffered lane models SYSREF sent through plain buffers, for comparison only.

    One clock does both jobs. The chain carries a single 5 MHz clock, the SYSREF rate. In DZ each card LMK04828 locks to it in nested zero-delay mode with the SYSREF divider as feedback, so every module makes its own SYSREF with one fixed phase to the incoming edge.

    No SYSREF cable runs between modules, and no module samples another module's SYSREF. In TS5 the same edge also reaches the card SYNC pin once, through U22 and the U61 gate, and the card runs zero-delay with DCLKout8 feedback (UG1437 p.10).

    Modules are numbered from the root: module k sits k hops after module 0. The GTY reference does not ride on the chain: each card loops its own J32 (250 MHz) back through carrier J45, in every profile. Only the card-only chain uses J32 for the chain clock.

    Delay. Each hop adds a buffer and a cable: 300 mm of coax, the W20 and W17 pigtails inside the two boxes, plus one LMK00804B (U28, 1–2.2 ns, check). That delay is fixed, so calibration removes it with a start offset in 4 ns steps plus a fine trim.

    Drift. Every buffer in the path drifts with temperature, and the last module sees the sum: k·α·ΔT in the worst case, √k·α·ΔT for independent hops. The MON_CLK edge monitor tracks it in service.

    Jitter. Buffer additive jitter adds in quadrature on the reference: σref(k) = √(σ0² + k·σbuf²), with σ0 100 fs (source placeholder) and σbuf 20 fs per LMK00804B hop (estimate, larger at slow splitter edges): 100 / 102 / 106 / 113 fs for 0 / 1 / 3 / 7 hops.

    PLL1 (narrow loop) filters reference jitter above its bandwidth, so the output jitter (≈ 100 fs class) is set by the card VCXO and PLL2. What accumulates along a chain is slow wander and drift inside the PLL1 bandwidth (k·α·ΔT).

    Trigger. TRIG only has to land inside one 200 ns SYSREF period. In a chain each module's own edge comes (k − 1) hops later, and its arming margins are counted against that edge (PA.model.trig.margins, values in Sync & trigger). Above 4 modules use the active fan-out or the GNSS-armed start.

    True SYSREF on a chain (CHAIN-TS). The chain cables carry a true SYSREF too: each card samples the relayed 5 MHz edge once, on its own zero-delay VCO grid, so sampling points do not add up. A placement trim (DCLKout8 delay or half step, check) is scanned per module at commissioning.

    Failure. A chain depends on every module before it. U28 runs on the always-on U58 rail, so a module whose card is off still relays. A module with its 12 V off breaks the chain (there is no bypass relay), so re-cable around it.

    Card only (A1). J32 of one card, in SYSREF-divider mode at 5 MHz, drives J35 of the next through a DC block; R348 already terminates J35. TRIG comes from a ≤ 2.5 V, 50 Ω-source LVCMOS into J64 (A10 listens, LMK SYNC off) or from a GNSS start; no bare card can be TRIG master.

    The A1 root card runs PLL1 on a 5 MHz PL clock (CLKin2) or in holdover. Each card's SPI sync briefly stops its J32, so the cards sync strictly root → tail: bring-up takes about N × the PLL1 settle time. The GTY then runs from the card's free-running SI5341 (one-bit rows not locked to the DACs).

    Cables. The hop cables run between neighbouring rear panels: 250 mm on the bench and about 450 mm between rack shelves (estimate). 3D & mechanics shows the panels.

    Engineering notes Recommendation in full
    • Use the derived SYSREF (DZ) unless a true SYSREF is needed. It removes the SYSREF cable, every sampling window between modules and the LMK04832 output limit. TS5 runs on the same cables as a cross-check.
    • 2 to 8 modules in one rack: Master + splitter (MASTER-DZ). No box, 1U and about 10 W saved, one passive splitter and a resistive TRIG star (active fan-out above 4 modules). Every module sits one cable from the root, so no drift builds up.
    • True SYSREF wanted: MASTER-TS, or the sync unit (UNIT-TS). Every card already has the J64 SYSREF tweak, so both need only a different profile (if R699 cannot be reached, derived only); the sync unit also needs its own cables.
    • 2 to 4 modules side by side: the chain (CHAIN-DZ) is the alternative with the fewest cables. At 8 modules the drift over seven hops exceeds the one-bit UI (see the drift status), so use a star.
    • Card-only chain A1: for bring-up of bare cards. It uses up J32, so the GTY runs from the card's free-running SI5341 (one-bit rows not locked to the DACs).
    • Every carrier is identical. The clock zone (U20, U22 and U28 LMK00804B, Y1 + U29, U30, U59, U60, U61) makes any module root, relay, leaf or tail by software. U21, JP1, JP3, J40, J41, J43, K1 and E2 are gone.
    • Prefer a star when modules sit far apart, at 8 modules, when one module must be serviced while the others run, or when the skew target is below about 30 ps without re-calibration. Use the card-only chain on the lab bench.

    Details Multi-board signals

    Only the trigger is timing-critical between modules. It travels on coax into every module's rear-panel J28 and on through W19 and the carrier to the slot pin PERST# and FPGA D9: from the sync unit, from the TRIG master's J28 through a resistive star (N ≤ 4), an active fan-out in the kit (N > 4), or along a short bus in a chain. Everything else between modules (profiles, ready flags, latency reports, the common target latency) goes over Ethernet through the PC, where a few milliseconds do not matter.

    D9 goes through a 2-flip-flop synchroniser and arms only on 4 consecutive high samples at 125 MHz, so a reflection cannot arm twice. U62 keeps another module's TRIG master from back-powering an unpowered D9. TRIG margins and the DC level at D9: Sync & trigger status.

    Assumptions Model, formulas and what the bound assumes
    • Series coupling capacitor between a matched 50 Ω source and a 50 Ω load: fc = 1 / (2π (RS + RL) C), 100 Ω in total: 0.22 µF → 7.23 kHz, 1 µF → 1.59 kHz, 10 µF → 159 Hz. Capacitors in one loop combine in series first: card 0.22 µF + C1 1 µF → 8.83 kHz.
    • Shunt choke: fc = (RS ∥ RL) / (2π L) = 25 Ω / (2π L): 4 µH → 995 kHz, 133 µH → 29.9 kHz, staged 1.104 mH → 3.6 kHz. The carrier stages its chokes, 4 µH + 100 µH + 1 mH ≈ 1.104 mH: the small one covers the high end, the large one the low end.
    • Source edge defaults (estimates): GTY 20 ps at 20 Gb/s, RF-DAC 60 ps; the edge enters as one pole at 0.35 / tedge. A single-ended path has no balun, so the balun select is off there.
    • Primary estimate (solid): exact −3 dB of the cascaded passive poles, the source edge as one pole (0.35 / tedge, estimate), the DAC sinc on DAC paths and the interconnect loss at the longest length (the shaded band spans best to worst length).
    • Baluns, the amplifier, PE43711 and FL1 are known only by their data-sheet ranges. They are drawn as bars, not poles; a range end is where the vendor stops specifying, not a measured −3 dB point.
    • Bound under assumption (dashed): the range ends used as first-order −3 dB corners. Real parts usually reach past their ranges, so real rise and droop are smaller; the bound never sets a status.
    • Status levels come from specified ranges and exact poles only: FAIL when a range excludes the target, CHECK when a block is not modelled or chosen, the target sits at a range end, or loss data are unverified.
    • Droop over τ: D = 1 − exp(−2π Σ fL τ); a 1 MHz corner costs 0.314 % over 500 ps, so short pulses pass AC coupling well. The low corner matters for long pulses, slow DC-level steps and long patterns. Rise time 10–90 % ≈ 0.35 / BW; rise and fall are equal in this linear model.
    • Output power for a peak Vpk into 50 Ω: sine-equivalent 10·log10(Vpk² / (2 · 50 Ω) / 1 mW) = 19.54 dBm at 3.00 V; rectangular high level Vpk² / 50 Ω = 22.55 dBm; average at 0.50 % duty −0.46 dBm.
    • Interconnect: α(f) = a·√f + b·f dB per mm. Lanes and D0–D7: a and b to be fitted to the stack-up and cable data (placeholders today, so the HF status stays CHECK). RF-DAC outputs add the W1–W8 pigtail (0.047 in class figures) with its SMPM pair and SMA bulkhead (≈ 0.1 dB each at 5 GHz), all check; the one-bit outputs are a direct PCB-edge launch. The GTY TX FIR can pre-emphasise lane loss (not modelled).
    • Time domain: a discrete-time cascade of first-order sections in periodic steady state (no S-parameters, no ringing). DAC paths keep the 60 ps edge estimate there; the sinc is applied in the frequency plot only. The pulse period is the frame period of the rate preset (100 ns).
    • The real edge and the real low end are to measure: the bound is pessimistic, the estimate leaves out what the data sheets do not give.

    Parts on the boards: Carrier schematic (T1, L1 / L2 / L5, C1–C5 on the one-bit outputs; C11, L10–L12 on the DAC outputs) and Card findings (the card DAC path).

    Cost trade-off Two parameters we give up to save money
    • Output swing headroom (−3 dB). The next carrier combines the one-bit P and N legs in the balun first and amplifies once, with the same amplifier part as the RF-DAC chain, instead of one amplifier per leg. Two amplifiers combined in the balun give 3 dB more output power; we give that up. One chain per channel needs 2 amplifiers instead of 4 and one bias tee instead of two.
    • Lowest usable frequency. One simple bias tee per output replaces the staged 4 µH + 100 µH + 1 mH chokes, so the low corner of each output rises above the 1 MHz target.

    Both cut the parts per channel, and a four-module array has 64 channels; the saving is significant, so we accept the loss.

    PASS · negligible

    After calibration the skew, plus the terms to measure, fits inside one one-bit step. Measure MTS, GTY and PLL1 offsets.

    Details Method: linear, RSS, worst case

    Deterministic and calibration residual add linearly (worst case); drift adds linearly over ΔT; random terms add in quadrature per path and stay in the fs panel.

    • Deterministic static terms and the calibration residuals add linearly (worst case).
    • Drift adds linearly over the stated ΔT (chain: k · α · ΔT).
    • Random jitter adds in quadrature (RSS) per path; between two modules σ grows by √2; peak to peak uses k = 6.
    • Random jitter is a spread around the mean, not an offset, so it is never stacked into the ps bars; it has its own fs panel.
    • The worst-case line adds 6σ of each path to the deterministic residual after calibration: 20.35 ps (DAC) / 20.49 ps (one-bit), plus the terms to measure.

    Lengths come from the geometry (card 235 mm); the inputs above override the model defaults for this view only.

    The RF-DAC outputs pass one identical W1–W8 pigtail (100 mm), so only its length tolerance (±2 mm × 4.8 ps/mm = ±9.6 ps) enters the budget; the one-bit outputs have no pigtail. A chain hop passes the W20 pigtail of one module and the W17 pigtail of the next (2 × 210 mm) on top of the external cable.

    Details Thermal

    Every watt ends up as heat in the box: 54.9 W per module. The airflow path (front inlet, card heatsink, rear fan) and the cooling notes are in 3D & mechanics.

    Details What stays the same, what changes

    The carrier design, the card prep (CLK on J35 as fitted, the one R699 micro-coax tweak for true SYSREF), the firmware image and the start-up sequence stay the same at every size. Every module is identical, so any module can be the root, and a spare can replace any other after a skew re-calibration and a new MTS run.

    What changes is outside the boxes: the external sync kit (splitter size, TRIG star or active fan-out, cable count), the switch size and the supply. With the sync unit and true SYSREF (UNIT-TS), 8 modules need 16 outputs (CLK + SYSREF) against the LMK04832's 14, so add buffers; UNIT-DZ needs 8. Supply size and rack space grow linearly.

    Card prices are the list price from the earlier comparison; quotes are still pending. The card price is set in the BOM.

    Details DAC-only modules

    If a module only needs RF-DAC outputs, leave the one-bit front ends unpopulated and skip the GTY rework. The 16-DAC option then costs two cards plus two lighter carriers. Set "DAC only" in the rail Configuration; the rack, supply and BOM follow.

    Details How to read the table

    Quantities are per carrier; cables, panels and the card prep are per module; the rack and system group is per system. The last column multiplies by the module count. Every module is built the same way for every sync option; the external sync kit is per system.

    Rows follow DAC only from the rail Configuration. DAC-only modules leave the one-bit group and J18–J25 unpopulated; caps close their eight D-flat holes on the rear panel.

    Select a row to see its details, its part card and, for parts on the carrier, a link to the board view. Parts counts add plain quantities only; rows counted in sets or marked "option" are left out. Costs are class estimates for prototype quantities, not quotes. Copy as CSV copies every row that matches the filter.

    Showing all 18 findings.
    ItemStatusImpact
    GTY to the edge
    Rework on card
    		Only 4 of 8 one-bit channels reach the carrier.
    Details As delivered · what we do

    As delivered. TX0–3 fitted through 0.22 µF. TX4–7 go to QSFP2 through 0 Ω; the edge capacitors for lanes 4–7 are not fitted.

    What we do. Rework 8 capacitors per card: fit C632–C635 and C1022–C1025, remove the QSFP2 TX links. The RX side is not needed. See the GTY rework checklist.

    GTY reference
    Fixed on carrier
    		Card J32 looped through the carrier locks the GTYs to the DACs.
    Details As delivered · what we do · card J32

    As delivered. The SI5341 runs from its own 48 MHz oscillator and makes 156.25 / 125 MHz for the GTY quads, so the GTYs drift against the DACs and against other modules. The edge PCIE_CLK pins go to quad A refclk1 through 10 nF.

    What we do. Loop the card's own J32 back through the carrier in every profile: J32 at 250 MHz (SDCLKout5, VCO ÷ 12, LVPECL 2000 mV format, check) → W23 → carrier J45 → C20 DC block → U27 (LMK1D1204, differential input mode: IN0_P terminated in 49.9 Ω, IN0_N AC-coupled to VAC_REF; it needs 0.3 Vpp and runs to 2 GHz, while its single-ended mode stops at 250 MHz) → PCIE_CLK (10 nF on the card) → quad A refclk1; quad B shares it. QPLL0 N = 40 gives 10 GHz and 20 Gb/s, and 250 MHz = 50 × 5 MHz gives one fixed phase to SYSREF. Release QPLL0 only after the card LMK has locked, synced and settled. W23 stays plugged in every profile; the carrier has no U21. Fallback: lock the SI5341 through its unused IN2 input (rework).

    Card J32. The card's only external clock output and its only SMA: LMK04828 SDCLKout5, single-ended, DC-coupled LVPECL (about 0.4–0.6 Vpp into 50 Ω, estimate), so every cable from it needs an inline DC block. Its clock group shares only DCLKout4 (ADC_REFCLK1, an RF-ADC tile we do not use), so J32 can run at VCO / 1…32 or from the SYSREF divider (5 MHz = ÷ 600). Only the bare-card chain A1 (bring-up, no carriers) uses J32 as a 5 MHz daisy-chain reference into the next card's J35; with carriers J32 is the GTY reference in every profile.

    Clock input J35 → CLKin1
    Stock, registers only
    		The shared 5 MHz enters on a stock connector, no FPGA in the path.
    Details As delivered · what we do

    As delivered. LMK04828 + 19.2 MHz VCXO U47. The SSMC-edge J35 "CLK1_IN" (column position 2, below J57 GNSS_ANT and J64 PPS_IN) → R345 0 Ω → R348 49.9 Ω shunt → C374 0.1 µF → CLKin1 (pin 34; pin 35 to ground through C373). The vendor firmware selects CLKin1 ("CLKIN1 EXTERNAL") but runs PLL1 open loop. The reference is there from carrier power-up.

    What we do. Carrier J32 → W21 → J35, AC-coupled (levels in Sync & trigger). Registers only: CLKin_SEL_MODE = 1, CLKin1_OUT_MUX = PLL1, bipolar input, CLKin0 off; our register file clears the vendor HOLDOVER_FORCE and MAN_DAC_EN and fixes OSCin_FREQ. Keep R345, R348, C374 and C373; re-fit R345 on any card prepared the old way. If the first card shows J35 on CLKin0, set CLKin_SEL_MODE = 0: still no rework. The default profile uses only J35: each card makes its own derived SYSREF and carrier U22 holds the SYNC pin low.

    J66, J67 and U48 absent
    No step
    		Nothing to fix; the old prep steps for them are dropped.
    Details As delivered · what we do

    As delivered. The V1 schematic draws J66 "CLK0_IN" → jumper J67 → CLKin0, with the 10 MHz TCXO U48 (DIP-14) on J67 pin 1. The real card has no J66 and no J67, and the U48 footprint is empty on the vendor photo. The old steps (J67 link, J66 pigtail, R340 removal) are dropped, and so are the J35 SMA and the R345 removal.

    What we do. No step. Confirm on the first card: J66 and J67 absent, U48 empty, J35 centre to the R344 node open.

    SYSREF tweak J64 → LMK SYNC
    Card prep
    		One build runs every profile: derived SYSREF, or a true SYSREF edge on J64.
    Details As delivered · what we do

    As delivered. J64 (SSMC, PPS_IN, column position 1) → R245 33 Ω → FPGA A10, R248 1 kΩ to ground, U127 TPD4E001 ESD, C212. The SYNC pin (pin 6, CMOS, VIH ≥ 1.2 V, VIL ≤ 0.4 V, 160 kΩ internal pull-down, abs max VCC + 0.3 V) hangs on K19 through R699.

    What we do. Remove R699. Fit one jacketed 50 Ω micro-coax (1.13 mm FEP; 0.81 mm only if jacketed, a bare outer would short the empty U101 pads) of one fixed length, set on the first card (45–70 mm expected) and held to ±2 mm (±9.6 ps). Centre from the J64 centre-finger joint to the LMK-side pad of R699; braid to a J64 ground finger and to one fixed ground pad chosen on the first card (candidate: the GND end of C904). Route it across the empty U101 footprint on Kapton with 2–3 RTV dots, clear of J32, the VCXO and the LMK outputs, from one template photo. Keep R245, R248, U127 and C212: A10 becomes an input-only SYSREF monitor (one edge per TS sync, none in DZ) and R248 holds pin 6 low with W22 unplugged. Do not tap on the A10 side and do not short R245. J64 then takes only ≤ 2.5 V from a 50 Ω source; never drive it above 3.3 V. If R699 cannot be reached cleanly: no soldering, derived SYSREF only. See the card prep checklist.

    K19 is PS_MIO26
    Card prep
    		The 3.3 V LMK outputs overdrive the 1.8 V MIO bank: firmware rule.
    Details As delivered · what we do

    As delivered. K19 is PS_MIO26 (bank 501, 1.8 V), a PS GPIO, not a PL pin. CLKin_SEL0 (R694) → PS_MIO33 and CLKin_SEL1 (R698) → PS_MIO34; SDO on Status_LD2 (R628) → PS_MIO36, all through 0 Ω from the 3.3 V LMK. The stock SYNC can only be toggled in software timing, which SPI SYNC_POL already does.

    What we do. Firmware, the same on every card: MIO26 input, never driven (R699 is removed anyway). MIO33 / 34 inputs: CLKin_SEL_MODE = 1 picks CLKin1 by register, so the SEL pins are unused. SPI readback on MIO36 open drain with the MIO pull-up and SCK ≤ 1 MHz (check). Read lock state over SPI (RB_PLL1_LD, RB_PLL2_LD). Vendor demos that held SYSREF_REQ high through MIO26 use the SPI pulser (SYNC_MODE = 3) or continuous SYSREF (SYSREF_MUX = 3) instead.

    PLL1 loop at a 5 MHz PFD
    Decide
    		Zero-delay static offset is unspecified: bench gate (status above).
    Details As delivered · what we do

    As delivered. Card loop filter C389 15 nF, R335 180 kΩ, C390 330 pF, C388 100 pF with VCXO U47 19.2 MHz (part number unknown); vendor PLL1 charge pump 1550 µA at a 160 kHz PFD.

    Impact. Every multi-module profile runs PLL1 at a 5 MHz PFD in nested zero-delay (VCXO-to-PFD ratio 3.84, loop gain ≈ 31× higher). The offset per nA of leakage is in the PLL1 status above; TI does not specify the leakage, so it is to measure.

    What we do. Bench gate, likely a change: Icp 1550 µA in zero-delay with C388 / C389 / C390 × ≈ 31 and R335 ÷ ≈ 31 (≈ 3.3 nF / 470 nF / 10 nF / 5.6 kΩ), a low Icp in dual-loop. Final values from PLLatinum Sim and the U47 VCTL data, one identical change on every card in the same session as the SYSREF tweak. The settle time sets the wait before MTS.

    PL clock vs DAC AXI clock
    Card firmware
    		PL_CLK 125 MHz keeps the MTS clocks in integer ratios.
    Details As delivered · what we do

    As delivered. Our earlier plan used PL_CLK = 250 MHz (DCLKout8 ÷ 12). At 10 GS/s in DUC bypass the DAC AXI4-Stream clock is 625 MHz (16 samples per word): 625 / 250 = 2.5 is not an integer, so the RFdc IP cannot relate the clocks under MTS (PG269 p.190, p.224, p.359).

    What we do. PL_CLK = DCLKout8 ÷ 24 = 125 MHz; one MMCM makes × 5 = 625 MHz (DAC AXI) and × 2 = 250 MHz (fabric, GTY user clock). AXI clocks come from PL_CLK, never from clk_dacX (p.188). Vivado check before board work; fallbacks in Frequency plan.

    RF-DAC delay: coarse only
    Firmware rule
    		Sub-100 ps trims cannot come from the DAC tile.
    Details As delivered · what we do

    As delivered. Gen3 / DFE RF-DAC tiles have a coarse delay of 0–40 T1 (100 ps steps), applied through a SYSREF update event. There is no DAC fine delay (PG269 p.153, p.256). The MTS residual is not given in ps (to measure).

    What we do. Whole samples by PL pattern shift; coarse delay only through a SYSREF event. Sub-100 ps: DAC_REFCLK ADLY (25 ps steps, a bench decision on jitter), cable length or waveform shaping.

    Acceptance test per card
    Card prep
    		A card that misses a prep step breaks every profile it joins.
    Details Acceptance list

    As delivered. Not part of the vendor test.

    Power off. J64 centre ↔ LMK pin 6 ≈ 0 Ω; J64 centre ↔ the A10-side pad of R245 = 33 Ω and that node ↔ GND ≈ 1 kΩ; R699 K19-side pad ↔ pin 6 open; J35 centre ↔ R348 node 0 Ω (R345 present) and R348 ↔ GND 49.9 Ω; A11 finger ↔ the R242 pad nearest A11 ≈ 0 Ω, R304 absent; coax length logged.

    Power on. BENCH-DZ lock and 5 power cycles of MTS, one BENCH-TS sync with exactly 1 edge on A10 and 1 on MON_SYNC (C9), D9 drive and read through the slot. Record the card serial with the carrier EUI-48.

    First-card checks before soldering
    Check first
    		Where R699 sits decides whether the tweak repeats on every card.
    Details As delivered · what we do

    As delivered. The schematic is V1; the vendor photo shows silk "REVISION 2.1". R699, the J64 parts and the PERST# path are not yet seen on a real card. Rev 2.1 may change values or add a buffer on PERST# (the "_LS" net name).

    What we do. Photos and continuity on the first card, then a CLKin1 lock on J35, then the coax dry fit; after the tweak a probe or TDR check, the TS5 placement-trim scan and a QPLL0 check during a TRIG edge. If R699 is on the bottom side or cannot be reached cleanly, stop: derived SYSREF only. See the first-card checklist.

    PCIe connector rating (J1)
    Test before freeze · 3D & mechanics
    		A connector rated below 20 Gb/s closes the one-bit eye near 10 GHz.
    Details As delivered · what we do · pass targets

    As delivered. A standard x8 card edge. GTY TX0–7 cross J1 as one-bit lanes at 20 Gb/s (Nyquist 10 GHz), above the PCIe 3.0 and 4.0 line rates; extra loss, reflections and crosstalk there close the eye.

    What we do. J1 is a vertical x8 CEM socket rated PCIe Gen5 (32 GT/s), SMT preferred so it can be backdrilled; the part is still to confirm (status owned by 3D & mechanics). Before the carrier freezes: the vendor S-parameter model, a VNA / TDR coupon (10 MHz – 10 GHz) and a 20 Gb/s pulse test through the real connector. See Roadmap.

    Pass targets. S11 ≤ −15 dB and a smooth S21 to 5–6 GHz, S11 ≤ −10 dB to 8 GHz, adjacent-pair NEXT / FEXT ≤ −35 dB, clean edges at the one-bit cell input.

    No card bracket
    Check · 3D & mechanics
    		The slot alone would carry a 235 × 148 mm card with its heatsink and fan, and the QSFP / RJ45 plug forces would load the 20 Gb/s slot contacts.
    Details As delivered · what we do

    As delivered. A bare board on four white corner standoffs (vendor photos); no PCIe bracket. In the box the card I/O faces the front panel: its cut-out gives insertion clearance and the bolt-on I/O shield closes it; neither holds the card.

    What we do. The stock standoffs come off; four M3 standoffs (8 mm + 0.7 mm shim) run from the corner holes on the card back face to the right wall, M3 pan heads with washers outside the wall. The slot sets the card position; the slot latch stays and needs the retention notch on the card x8 tab (check on the first card). Card swap: lid and I/O shield off, cables off the card, the four wall screws out, pull the card up out of J1, slide it toward the rear and lift it out. Parts in the BOM (Card standoffs, Card fixings).

    Card measurements
    Check first
    		Card geometry comes from vendor photos (±3 %): measure before the carrier is released.
    Details As delivered · what we do

    As delivered. No mechanical drawing. Outline, connector places and part heights come from vendor photos (≈ 235 × 148 mm, ±3 %). The photos disagree on one hole (BR, u 228 / v 141.5, ≈ 2 mm into the RJ45).

    What we do. Measure the first card before the carrier is released: length (the box takes 225–320 mm), the SSMC-edge-to-finger offset (it places J1), the corner and finger tabs, finger protrusion (9.5 mm in the model, 10.5–12.5 mm from photos) and thickness (1.57 mm), the four hole positions (they carry the standoffs to the right wall; the bottom SSMC-edge hole may sit on the corner tab below ADC0) and the x8 tab retention notch, back-side part heights (≤ 2.67 mm assumed), heatsink fin type and direction, fan stack height (40 ± 5 mm) and the 12 V current at full load (the slot pins carry ≤ 66 W; above that fit J34 → P3). See 3D & mechanics.

    DAC outputs
    Rework on card
    		The card balun sets a 30 MHz lowest frequency.
    Details As delivered · what we do

    As delivered. 0.1 µF → TCM2-63WX+ → 0.1 µF → SSMC J44–J51. Unfitted resistor options sit around each balun. The balun is specified from 30 MHz; the capacitors alone allow much less (corner in the card blocks table of One module).

    What we do. Swap to UWB2-50E, or bypass to one leg. Build both versions to compare, as suggested in the requirements review. The resulting low-frequency limit of each path is in Analog frontend.

    GPIO
    OK as is
    		J65 is enough for carrier control; no new ribbon line.
    Details As delivered · what we do

    As delivered. J65 2×10 header: 10 GPIO (3.3 V HD bank) + I²C. PERST# on the edge goes to FPGA pin D9.

    What we do. The J65 ribbon is unchanged: IO3 = SYNC_GATE (out), IO8 = MON_SYNC and IO9 = MON_CLK (in), and the carrier's TCA9538 (0x70) switches the clock zone over I²C. PERST# now carries TRIG IO (next row).

    TRIG IO over PERST# → D9
    OK as is, check
    		TRIG needs no card work, and J64 stays free for SYSREF.
    Details As delivered · what we do · TRIG path

    As delivered. Edge finger A11 PERST# → net PCIE_PERST_B_LS_R → R242 0 Ω → PCIE_PERST → FPGA D9 (HD bank 88, 3.3 V). The R304 pull-up is not fitted (V1 sheet 2). No host resets the card, so the pin is free.

    What we do. D9 as IOBUF LVCMOS33, SLEW SLOW, DRIVE 8, pull-down, no PCIe IP bound to it. Rear-panel J28 → W19 → J28A → D11 TVS → 50 Ω trace → U62 isolation switch (on only while U59 reports card power good) → 33 Ω → slot A11 PERST# → R242 → D9; 10 kΩ idle low at J28A, 100 kΩ on the slot side (Carrier schematic). The TRIG master drives 60 ns after its own SYSREF edge; listeners arm on ≥ 4 consecutive high samples at 125 MHz. The DC level at D9 and the fan-out limit are in Sync & trigger.

    Check on the first card. A11 position (≈ u 58.6 mm, unverified), R242 = 0 Ω, R304 absent, no buffer on rev 2.1, and D9 driven and read through the slot. If rev 2.1 has a one-way buffer, listeners still read D9 and the master drives out on J65 IO7 through a small carrier gate.

    J57 GNSS and J64 PPS_IN
    OK as is
    		J64 becomes the SYSREF entry; J57 stays free for a GNSS option.
    Details As delivered · what we do · access

    As delivered. Schematic page 17. J64 (SSMC, PPS_IN) → R245 33 Ω → FPGA pin A10 (3.3 V HD bank), R248 1 kΩ to ground, TPD4E001 ESD. J57 (SSMC) → NEO-M8N RF_IN, antenna bias from VCC_RF through L40 10 nH; the TIMEPULSE goes only to FPGA pin A9 (GNSS_PPS), not to the LMK. U101 (the NEO-M8N) is not fitted on the stock card.

    Impact. J64 becomes the true SYSREF entry (the tweak above) and A10 an input-only monitor; the PPS_IN function is given up. GNSS gives time of day and a PPS of tens-of-ns class (check the datasheet), not a ps clock reference, and needs U101.

    What we do. J57 stays free: position 0 is clear for an antenna plug. For a GNSS-armed start, fit U101 on every card as an identical option; the SYNC coax then re-routes below its outline and is re-measured. The antenna (or a GNSS splitter arm) reaches J57 on the SSMC edge, ≈ 32 mm inside the rear panel: rear access cover for J57 and ADC1–8 (cables through its brush-strip slot / Ø6 hole with the cover on; cover off to plug). GNSS-armed start: the antenna cable reaches J57 through the rear access cover; no internal GNSS cable. A lab PPS enters J28 → D9. See Sync & trigger.

    Power
    OK as is
    		The card runs from the carrier's 12 V.
    Details As delivered · what we do

    As delivered. 12 V through the edge fingers and the P3 connector. The VCCINT regulator is rated 40 A.

    What we do. Feed the slot 12 V pins (≤ 66 W by the PCIe spec) and / or cable to P3. Check the real card power in XPE; the module total is in Power.

    One carrier build for every module; open: DC level polarity, LF limit: HMC788A.

    Details Layout rules 1–5
    1. One-bit cells next to J1. The eight one-bit cells (one can, 15 mm pitch) sit between J1 and the rear edge, so each output launches straight into its row A jack; the RF-DAC cells sit beyond the lane corridor (their signals arrive over D0–D7); lanes 50–158 mm.
    2. Matched 100 Ω pairs. ±0.1 mm inside each pair; lanes matched to ±0.5 mm where the layout allows, the rest is a fixed offset taken out by calibration (Timing & skew).
    3. Short strips to the output jacks. One-bit: each cell ends at its own bulkhead-type PCB jack on the rear edge (row A), no internal RF cable. RF-DAC: each cell ends at a vertical SMPM (J10A–J17A); one identical pigtail (W1–W8) runs to its rear-panel bulkhead (row B).
    4. Separate DC ground return. The DC-level buffers U33–U40 return on their own path, so DC current stays out of the RF ground under the amplifiers.
    5. Sync striplines on an inner layer. Between ground planes and clear of the one-bit via fields. The clock zone sits at the rear next to J26A–J29A: J26A / J27A → U20 / U22 ≈ 12 mm, U20 / U22 → carrier J32 / J33 ≈ 14–26 mm (estimate).
    Details Clock zone behaviour
    • U30 TCA9538 sets every clock source over I²C (0x70 on every carrier). Its pins start Hi-Z, so the pulls set safe defaults: U20 off, U22 off (SYNC low), U28 relaying, LOCAL5 and Y1 off.
    • Root, relay, leaf and tail are U30 register settings in the profile the PC sends. No straps, one build.
    • U59 watches the card 3.3 V: it holds U20 and U22 off while the card is off and resets U30 each time.
    • U58, the always-on 3.3 V ahead of U50, keeps U28 relaying a chain while the card or the main rails are off. A module with its 12 V off still breaks a chain.
    • U20, U22 and U28 take square inputs, 0.35–1.8 Vpp, 5 or 10 MHz; open inputs idle low. The level per sync option is in Sync & trigger.
    • W21, W22 and W23 are fixed in every profile; the sync jacks J26–J29 sit on the rear panel (row C) and reach J26A–J29A over W17–W20.
    Details Placement and stack-up

    Carrier: 160 × 267 mm, 8 layers, RF on the top face, rear edge 1.0 mm inside the rear panel (row A clamp faces)

    Stack-up: 8 layers: L1 top parts, L2 GND, L3 GTY lanes (100 Ω), L4 GND, L5 power, L6 REFCLK / TRIG / sync striplines, L7 GND, L8 bottom parts; continuous ground, no splits

    Faces: top: one-bit can and RF-DAC can (RF on the top face), J1, sideband pocket, clock zone, power entry, LDOs, bucks, control; bottom: one-bit bias-choke stages (100 µH + 1 mH, 6 × 6 × 3.5 mm) under the cells, SMT spacers; nothing taller than 6 mm (floor gap 10.5); no jacks.

    • one-bit band: one 8-cavity can at 15 mm pitch (1BIT1 … 1BIT8 at x +61 … −44), direct edge launch into row A (J18–J25)
    • RF-DAC band: one 8-cavity can z −61 … −13, outputs J10A–J17A (vertical SMPM) at z −63.5, inputs J2–J9 (vertical SSMC) at z −10
    • lane corridor (L3) in front of the one-bit cell inputs
    • lane bundle (L3) beside J1: TX0–TX3 run down to the corridor; no through-vias of other blocks
    • TX4–TX7 escape (L3) in front of the sideband pocket, then 45° under the DAC can
    • digital: J1 (vertical x8, Gen5-rated) and the GTY lane bundle
    • sideband pocket: U62 + R_T 33 Ω (TRIG → A11), J45 (W23) + C20 + U27 (REFCLK → A13 / A14); REFCLK and TRIG on L6 under the lane layer
    • clock zone: Y1, U29, U30 and the PLL loop filters in the rear half (z −6 … +14); U20, U22, U28; J26A–J29A (vertical SMPM, TVS each) and J32 / J33 (vertical SMA) at x ≤ +25; GND via fence at x +52
    • LDO / sequencer band (buffer between the clock zone and the bucks)
    • control zone: J31 (ribbon from card J65), U31–U48
    • bucks (RF-tagged: from z +62 at the rear to the carrier front − 3; ≥ 57 mm at L 225)
    • power entry: J46, F1, D12 TVS, U50 eFuse, bulk, common-mode choke; GND via fence at x −54; chassis bond at (−74, −128); no switching parts

    RF outputs: one-bit straight into the rear-panel row A jacks J18–J25; RF-DAC over the W1–W8 pigtails to the row B bulkheads J10–J17; sync from the row C bulkheads over W17–W20. Source: PA.model.geom.get('upright', L), the same data as the board view in 3D & mechanics.

    1. P0

      Evaluate one card

      2–4 weeks0 of 14 done

      Prove that one HamGeek card does what the design assumes before we draw the carrier.

      • Details: First-card checks

        Before any soldering, on the first delivered card: photos and continuity for J35 → R345 → R348 → C374 → CLKin1, where R699 sits and its LMK-side pad, J64 → R245 / R248, A11 → R242 → D9 with R304 not fitted, J66, J67, U48 and U101 absent, and rev 2.1 against the V1 schematic; then a CLKin1 lock on J35 with our registers. If R699 cannot be reached cleanly, every profile runs derived SYSREF with no soldering.

        Card findings

      • Details: Vivado 125 / 625 MHz

        RFdc IP in Advanced mode with 10 GS/s DUC bypass, 16 samples per word, MTS on and PL clock 125 MHz: the GUI and DRC accept it, 625 MHz closes timing on the −2 part, and the DS926 AXI4-Stream maximum allows it. If not, switch to VCO0 2500 MHz or 8 GS/s.

        Frequency plan DS926↗ PG269↗

      • Details: Measure the card

        The card geometry comes from vendor photos (±3 %). On the first card: length (the box takes L 225–320 mm), the corner tab, finger protrusion and thickness (1.57 mm), the four corner holes for the M3 wall standoffs (photo estimates), the SSMC-edge-to-finger offset (u 48.6–101.5 mm), back-side part heights (≤ 2.67 mm assumed).

        Card measurement row

      • Details: 12 V current through J1

        Measure the card current at full load against the J1 12 V pin rating after derating; above it fit the optional J34 → P3 lead. The budget is the "Card 12 V supply" status in Power.

        Power status

      • Details: Fin direction, fan stack

        On the first card: heatsink fin type (plate or cross-cut) and direction, and the fan stack height (40 ± 5 mm). They set the airflow from the front inlet over the card heatsink to the rear 60 mm fan (thermal notes in 3D & mechanics).

        Thermal notes

      • Details: Vivado accepts PL_CLK 125 MHz with the 625 MHz AXI clock

        Vivado accepts PL_CLK 125 MHz against the 625 MHz DAC AXI4-Stream clock under MTS (PG269 p.190 says "integer", p.224 and p.359 "common integer multiple"), and 625 MHz closes timing on XCZU67DR-2. Fallbacks: VCO0 2500 MHz with PL_CLK 625 MHz, or 8 GS/s with 500 MHz.

        Frequency plan PG269 p.190↗ PG269 p.224↗ PG269 p.359↗

      • Details: GTY TX4–7 to the PCIe edge, 8 capacitors per card

        GTY TX4–7 to the PCIe edge (8 capacitors per card). Ask HamGeek whether they can ship cards with this option fitted.

        Card findings

      • Details: First card: clock, SYSREF and TRIG paths by photo and continuity

        First card, by photos and continuity before soldering: J35 → R345 → R348 → C374 → CLKin1 (not CLKin0), where R699 sits (top or bottom side) and its LMK-side pad, J64 → R245 / R248, A11 → R242 → D9 with R304 not fitted and no buffer on rev 2.1, J66, J67, U48 and U101 absent, CLKin_SEL0/1 via R694/R698 to MIO33/34, SDO via R628 to MIO36, DCLKout6 → tile 227 and DCLKout12 → tile 228. Check that our firmware can own the LMK SPI.

        First-card checklist XCZU67DR_PCIE_V1.pdf p.17

      • Details: PLL1 loop filter at a 5 MHz PFD

        PLL1 loop filter at a 5 MHz PFD (effective ratio 3.84): the zero-delay offset is I_leak / Icp × 200 ns, so a larger charge pump shrinks it; likely Icp 1550 µA with the filter scaled ≈ ×31 (PLLatinum Sim plus the U47 VCTL data). One identical change on every card; bench gate on the offset over ΔT 10–20 °C and 20+ power cycles. The offset per nA is the status in Card findings.

        PLL1 offset row TI PLLatinum Sim↗

      • Details: GTY quad B on quad A refclk1 at 20 Gb/s

        That GTY quad B can use quad A's refclk1 (PCIE_CLK) for QPLL0 at 20 Gb/s, and that the 10 nF edge coupling passes 250 MHz cleanly (UG578 refclk-sharing rules).

        UG578↗

      • Details: J32 as GTY reference: level at J45, U27 margin

        J32 as GTY reference: amplitude and slew at J45 after the DC block with J32 set to LVPECL 2000 mV, the margin of U27 (LMK1D1204) in differential input mode (its single-ended mode stops at 250 MHz), and that the GTY QPLL is released only after the card LMK reports lock and has settled.

        J32 as GTY reference datasheet↗

      • Details: Measure the first card before the carrier is drawn

        Measure the first card before the carrier is drawn: length, tab outline, finger protrusion and thickness, hole positions, back-side part heights, heatsink fins and fan stack height, and the 12 V current at full load. The box also needs the four corner holes for the M3 wall standoffs and the SSMC-edge-to-finger offset (u 48.6–101.5 mm).

        Card assumptions

      • Details: Single-leg bypass around each TCM2-63WX+

        Whether the unfitted resistors around each TCM2-63WX+ allow a clean single-leg bypass, and how the DAC output gets its DC bias in that case.

        Analog frontend datasheet↗

      • Details: Rate preset as one shared setting

        Open user decision (spec H.8 item 4). Default: the rate preset is one shared setting (freqPreset) that drives every timing graphic on this page. Alternative: a rate selector local to the Pulse generation stage only.

        Pulse generation

      Exit gate. Vivado accepts the clock plan (or a fallback is chosen). Eight GTY lanes run at 20 Gb/s, the DAC path is measured and the balun choice is written down. PLL1 locks on J35, TRIG works both ways over PERST# / D9, and MTS repeats on the prepped card.

      Details P0 tasks and stages
      • Run the Vivado check first: RFdc IP with PL_CLK 125 MHz and a 625 MHz DAC AXI4-Stream clock from one MMCM (milestone 2).
      • Run the first-card checks before any soldering (milestone 1, checklist).
      • Bring up one HamGeek card: power, JTAG, PCIe and the RF-DAC tiles.
      • Lock the LMK04828 PLL1 to an external 5 MHz CLK on J35 (CLKin1, CLKin_SEL_MODE = 1), with no rework.
      • Test TRIG IO on PERST# → D9 in both directions through a slot or riser: drive D9 and check the edge at A11, then drive A11 and read D9.
      • Optional: GNSS needs U101 (NEO-M8N), which is not fitted on the stock card. With U101 on a test card, fit an active antenna on J57, read GNSS time and check the PPS on FPGA pin A9.
      • Do the one-time card prep on that card (checklist: R699 out, the fixed-length J64 → SYNC micro-coax, MIO settings) and check MTS repeatability over power cycles with derived SYSREF and with one gated SYSREF edge on J64 (milestone 5).
      • Program J32 to 250 MHz and lock the GTY QPLL from it through the carrier buffer; confirm the GTY-to-SYSREF phase repeats over power cycles.
      • Run GTY TX0–3 at 20 Gb/s raw (QPLL0 N = 40) from that 250 MHz refclk on the PCIE_CLK pins.
      • Do the TX4–7 rework (fit C632–35 and C1022–25, remove the QSFP2 0 Ω parts) and repeat the 20 Gb/s test.
      • Measure the card DAC path (0.1 µF, TCM2-63WX+, SSMC) from 100 kHz to 6 GHz.
      • Decide between the UWB2-50E balun swap and the single-ended bypass.

    2. P1

      Carrier prototype

      One module0 of 19 done

      Turn one card into a working module: 3 V outputs into 50 Ω with a DC level on every channel, and the bench sync profiles proven.

      • Details: LMK00804B inputs

        AC-coupled single-ended drive with the offset bias: clean switching from 0.25 to 1.3 Vpp at 5 and 10 MHz, no chatter at the kit levels 0.521 (1:4), 0.328 (1:2 + 1:4), 0.207 (legacy 1:2 + 1:2 + 1:4), 1.168 Vpp (chain hop), idle low with nothing connected, and the J26 stub shared by U20 and U28.

        Sync inputs datasheet↗

      • Details: BENCH-DZ repeat

        Lock, settle time and phase of PL_CLK, PL_SYSREF and the MTS latency repeat over 20+ power cycles with the dual-loop-first divider sync. Measure the dual-loop ambiguity (≥ 4 positions, ≈ 83 ps apart) once on the same card.

        Sync & trigger

      • Details: J64 tweak edge check

        On the first reworked card, a ≥ 1 GHz probe or TDR at the R699 LMK-side pad shows one monotonic 0.4–1.2 V transit with no re-crossing of 1.2 V. The simulation behind the J64-side tap is idealised.

        Card prep

      • Details: TS5 single edge, trim

        Exactly one SYNC edge per sync on A10 and on MON_SYNC; SYNC_1SHOT_EN = 1 and SYNC_DIS8 = 1 keep the DCLKout8 feedback divider running while the others reset, then SYNC_DISX = 1 and SYSREF_MUX = 3 (to check against UG1437); PL_SYSREF sits ≥ 1.5 ns from every PL_CLK edge. Scan the placement trim per module (DCLKout8 delay or half step; check that FB_MUX taps after it), park mid-window and re-check with the carrier hot.

        Sync steps UG1437↗ datasheet↗

      • Details: PLL1 offset

        PLLatinum Sim at a 5 MHz PFD with the U47 VCTL data; likely Icp 1550 µA in zero-delay with the filter scaled ≈ ×31. Measure the CLKin1-to-SYSREF offset over ΔT 10–20 °C and 20+ power cycles before claiming < 100 ps. Any change is made the same on every card before the card prep is frozen.

        Skew budget TI PLLatinum Sim↗

      • Details: TRIG over PERST#

        On the first carrier (or a riser): D9 drives slot A11 and A11 drives D9 through U62, U62 follows card power good, and a TRIG edge on A11 causes no QPLL0 or one-bit lane error (REFCLK sits two pins away).

        GPIO path

      • Details: J1 Gen5 vertical socket: part and footprint

        Before the carrier freezes. J1: PCIe Gen5 (32 GT/s) vertical x8, part to confirm, SMT preferred (backdrillable). Confirm the part, its footprint and housing height, and the slot centre on the card plane; then the vendor S-parameter model, a VNA/TDR coupon (10 MHz–10 GHz) and a pulse test through the real connector. Pass: S11 ≤ −15 dB and a smooth S21 to 5–6 GHz, S11 ≤ −10 dB to 8 GHz, adjacent-pair NEXT/FEXT ≤ −35 dB, clean edges at the one-bit cell inputs.

        J1 details datasheet

      • Details: Lane escape DFM

        TX0–TX7 leave the J1 tails toward −x on an inner layer under the housing; TX4–TX7 run at 45° under the DAC can on L3 (its fences are L1–L2 microvias). Ask the fab before layout freeze (backdrill, microvias). Lane lengths come from the geometry (3D & mechanics).

        Board view

      • Details: Card retention and insertion fit

        On the first box: the four M3 wall standoffs (8 mm + 0.7 mm shim) line up with the measured corner holes and the J1 latch holds; during the insertion slide the SSMC barrels clear the rear panel (≥ 1 mm) and the switch lever and QSFP cages stay inside the front I/O cut-out.

        Card assumptions

      • Details: Rear panel fit: nuts, pigtails

        Solder J18–J25 with the rear panel (or a CNC copy with the same holes) bolted at the seated position; then check the nut + lock-washer torque on rows A–C, the W1–W8 and W17–W20 pigtail dress on the tie bar, and ≥ 12 mm of extraction-tool space above every SMPM.

        Rear panel

      • Details: Closed-lid thermal test

        On the first module with the lid on and the card at full load. The Tj estimate is the thermal status in 3D & mechanics (θsa and fan flow are typical figures). The test checks the flow from the front inlet through the card heatsink to the rear 60 mm fan, with the RF cans in it, and picks the fan part and its noise.

        Thermal notes

      • Details: J1 rating against 20 Gb/s lanes

        J1 rating against 20 Gb/s lanes. J1 is a vertical x8 CEM socket rated PCIe Gen5 (32 GT/s), SMT and backdrillable: confirm the part, then S-parameters and a 20 Gb/s pulse test before the carrier freezes (mech gate "J1 Gen5 vertical socket").

        J1 details datasheet

      • Details: LMK00804B CLK_EN timing, levels and pulls

        LMK00804B (SNAS642A): CLK_EN timing (can it pass exactly one pulse), tPD, VDD 3.3 V with VDDO 2.5 V on U22, OE Hi-Z behaviour and the internal pulls. The input network takes square 5 or 10 MHz sources at 0.35–1.8 Vpp.

        Sync inputs datasheet↗

      • Details: Power sequencing of U59, U30 and U61

        Power sequencing of U59, U30 and U61: card off → U20 / U22 Hi-Z within µs; card on → safe defaults until the PS writes U30; FPGA reconfiguration does not open the SYNC gate; TCA9538 behaviour with the card's I²C powered down.

        Carrier schematic datasheet↗ datasheet↗

      • Details: DAC_REFCLK ADLY for sub-100 ps trims

        DAC_REFCLK ADLY for sub-100 ps trims: measure its extra jitter at the 10 GS/s tile PLL input. If acceptable, enable it at mid-code on every card in every profile; if not, trim by cable length or waveform shaping (the RF-DAC has no fine delay, PG269 p.153).

        Skew budget PG269 p.153↗

      • Details: Gain blocks and PA at low frequency

        Gain-block and PA candidates at low frequency. Most "0.01–10 GHz" parts get their low corner from external bias parts, so confirm it with the staged chokes on a test board.

        Analog frontend datasheet↗

      • Details: Low-frequency target: 1 MHz, 30 kHz or DC

        Low-frequency target. 1 MHz fails today: the HMC788A is specified from 10 MHz and limits both one-bit paths (balun and single-ended), so 1 MHz needs an amplifier specified below 1 MHz in its place; the RF-DAC path as delivered stops at the TCM2-63WX+ (from 30 MHz), so it also needs the UWB2-50E swap (from 500 kHz). The passive corners already reach 11.3 kHz (one-bit) and 25.2 kHz (RF-DAC), estimate. 30 kHz also needs every balun and amplifier specified below it (the UWB2-50E stops at 500 kHz: a single-ended path or a lower balun) and staged chokes; true DC needs a separate DC-coupled design. The limit per path is the LOW-FREQUENCY RESPONSE status in Analog frontend.

        Analog frontend status

      • Details: DC-level range and polarity

        DC-level range and polarity. This sets whether the AD5675R plus an offset is enough, or whether we need a bipolar DAC.

        datasheet↗

      • Details: Interconnect loss data: D0–D7 cable and stack-up

        Open user decision (spec H.8 item 5). The D0–D7 micro-coax part and the carrier stack-up are not chosen, so the interconnect loss in the AFE chain uses placeholder data and the pulse-bandwidth status stays CHECK until the cable and laminate are supplied or approved. The W1–W8 pigtail (0.047 in hand-formable class) and its SMPM and SMA bulkhead losses are class figures to confirm with the chosen parts.
